R1_human_readable.rationale: The PRD clearly explains the agency portfolio, audiences, core flows, visual experience, content, surfaces, and expected behavior in coherent human-readable language.

R2_markdown_formatting.rationale: Headings, nested lists, tables, inline code, and section hierarchy are consistently structured and readable as Markdown.

R3_no_replica_original.rationale: The document neither frames the product as a replica nor catalogs features omitted relative to another site.

R4_no_implementation.rationale: Technical details remain product-facing visual, accessibility, behavior, route, and root-level asset requirements; the PRD does not prescribe source files, frameworks, packages, build commands, or code internals.

R5_no_submission_artifacts.rationale: No Web Craft workflow, validation pipeline, companion deliverable, review artifact, or submission file is referenced.

R6_scaffold_structure.rationale: The PRD contains all expected scaffold areas, with extensive requirements organized under Product Surfaces and a separate, comparatively compact Acceptance Criteria section.

W1_run_on_structure.rationale: Although detailed, the document uses nested lists and tables effectively; long catalog and biography rows remain coherent structured records.

W2_screenshot_references.rationale: No screenshots, screenshot folders, or screenshot filenames are referenced.

W3_section_content_placement.rationale: Global reusable catalogs and asset mappings are appropriately centralized, local requirements remain under their surfaces, and acceptance criteria provide verification without reproducing the complete surface specification.

W4_extra_sections.rationale: All top-level sections match the expected scaffold areas; additional headings are appropriately nested subsections.

summary.overall_rationale: The PRD is a complete, readable, correctly structured standalone product specification. It contains no replica framing, submission artifacts, disallowed implementation documentation, screenshot references, misplaced major content, or non-standard top-level sections.
